sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Cassis is a small tourist town whose problem is the summer, and the policy is to keep cars out of the centre and the calanques. The town says parking is paid every day of the year, with a red zone (Parking Savon) paid from 7am to 7pm and limited to three hours a day, and an orange street zone paid from 9am to 7pm; the post-parking charge is 25 euros in the red zone and 35 euros a day in the orange zone [0]. The town says parking in the centre is often saturated and advises following the signs to the free Gorguettes park-and-ride, with shuttles to the centre [7]. The tourist office adds that in high season the centre becomes saturated and recommends avoiding the 11am-3pm rush [8]. The Calanques National Park says parking in Cassis is very difficult, advises against driving into the centre or to the Presqu'île car park, especially in summer, and recommends the free Gorguettes park-and-ride plus the shuttle to the park entrance at Port-Miou [10]. Access to the park is restricted from 1 June to 30 September because of fire risk, and roads to Sormiou, Morgiou and Callelongue are closed to motor traffic on a schedule from the Easter holidays [12].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Métropole presented a reorganised Cassis bus network on 7 July 2025: shuttle 372 (Gorguettes to the centre) every 15 minutes and until midnight in summer, and a seasonal shuttle 373 serving the Presqu'île, with three new electric minibuses [13]. The town's page says line 372 runs from 9am to midnight every day in July and August, at weekends and holidays outside the summer, and in October and until 11 November only at weekends and long weekends, with no service on the day of the Marseille-Cassis race [9]. For that race on 25 October 2026 the town has announced restrictions on parking at Gorguettes and on the nearby roads [15]. A 1,500 cubic-metre water reservoir under construction by the Métropole disrupts access in the Port-Miou sector until June 2027, according to the Calanques National Park, in a notice that extends an earlier one [16]. Works at the Casino entrance run from 24 August to 30 November 2026 [14]. A summer evening Port-Miou shuttle runs from 1 July to 31 August [17]. The tourist office lists 54 charging spaces across the five town-centre car parks [6].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Interparking runs five car parks in Cassis: Viguerie (293 spaces), Mimosas (404), Madie (150), Bestouan (117) and Daudet (89) [1]. At Viguerie and Mimosas the first hour is free and, in high season, two hours cost 4.20 euros and a day 27.50 euros [2]; Madie and Bestouan charge from the first 15 minutes [3]; at Daudet the first 30 minutes are free in high season and the first two hours in low season [4]. Online passes cost 27.50 euros a day and 495 euros for 30 days [5]. The tourist office describes the Presqu'île car park as having 400 spaces, charged in high season and about a 10-minute walk from Port-Miou [11].

Our data cover the five Interparking car parks, with capacities in the feed that are lower than the operator's for Mimosas (260 against 404) and Viguerie (170 against 293), measured since 24 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 29% on weekdays and 44% at weekends, weighted by the feed's 769 spaces, the reverse of a commuter pattern: Mimosas and Viguerie rose from 38% and 36% to 50% at weekends, and every car park reached full in single readings, mostly on Saturday mornings. This is the low season and the pressure the town describes for summer is not in the data. About four weeks.
